meta.title: Glossary of historical name forms
meta.note: Name forms only as given in the cited pages (read on the box copies: General History of Africa vols II, III, V; HD2011 intro, pp.1-7). Cite ids are registered in data/periods.json. term_ar only where a cited page prints the Arabic form (khartoum, port_sudan: QASIM_MAWSUA vol. 4, checked on page image), tagged [يحتاج تحقق] and queued; otherwise none supplied.

variants: 'Aethiopians' / 'Ethiopians' (Greek and Roman usage for the inhabitants)
entries.note_en: The Greeks, and later the Romans, called the inhabitants of Nubia 'Ethiopians' (GHA II p.231); GHA II p.298 speaks of the 'Aethiopians', 'as the inhabitants of the Kush empire were then generally called'.
The northern Nubian kingdom (Arabic, Nuba), with its capital at Faras; later united with Makuria (GHA III p.194).
The central Nubian kingdom (Arabic, Mukurra), with its capital at Old Dongola (GHA III p.194).
The southern Nubian kingdom, whose northern border lay between the Fifth and Sixth Cataracts, 'with its capital at Soba, in the vicinity of modern-day Khartoum' (GHA III p.196).
Name form only. Links to the Medjay and Blemmyes were removed: no checked source read.
The Funj sultanate, with its capital at Sennar.
The Keira (Kayra) dynasty of the Fur, who give Darfur its name. GHA V p.187: 'The Kayra sultanate flourished from about 1640 to 1874.'
entries.badge_note: Founding date: GHA V p.187 'about 1640' vs era start 1650 in data/periods.json.

entries.note_en: A small Muslim kingdom in the north-eastern Nuba Mountains that kept semi-autonomy after the Turco-Egyptian conquest; its royal family traces its origin to a Ja'ali holy man.
entries.badge_note: REPORTED applies to the origin story only: oral tradition, per HD2011 p.4.

entries.note_en: The state founded by the Mahdi's movement; Holt & Daly title the period 'The Mahdist State: 1881–98'.
The joint British-Egyptian regime over the territories south of Egypt, 1899–1955 per Holt & Daly, set up by Kitchener after Omdurman.
Medieval Muslim geographers' name for the belt of Africa south of the Sahara; Holt & Daly use 'eastern Bilad al-Sudan' for the lands south of Egypt.
Arabic form as printed in QASIM_MAWSUA vol. 4 ('جامعة الخرطوم', 'معهد الخرطوم الدولى').
